summary: Iteration 10 — stem-based content moderation verified end-to-end. BACKEND: extended /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py with TestModerationStemsIteration10 (43 new parametrized cases). All 43 new cases PASS: TRUE-positive coverage — 'Vendo Drog3' (user's original example), 'Drog4', 'dr0ga', 'drogaaa', 'v3nd3re Arm1', 'Vendita p1st0le', plus new iteration terms sesso/porno/orgia/alcol/alcool/alcohol/ubriac/stupefac/attentat/uccider/ammazz/omicid across title, description, location, category_label AND chat POST /api/groups/{id}/messages; TRUE-negative coverage — 'Cena carbonara', 'Corso di ceramica', 'Sessione di studio', 'Metodo di studio', 'Cocacola party', 'Hashtag social', 'Carmine e i suoi amici', 'Il gatto sul tetto', 'Un po d erba nel parco' are ALL accepted (200) — stem word-boundary correctly avoids false positives on inner substrings. Detail message wording exact-matches 'Contenuto non consentito: sono vietati riferimenti a droga, armi, violenza, sesso esplicito, alcol o contenuti illegali.'. Updated the FORBIDDEN_DETAIL constant in TestModerationGroups/TestModerationMessages to the new wording (was still on the old iteration 8/9 wording without 'sesso esplicito, alcol' — those pre-existing tests would otherwise have broken). FRONTEND (Expo web, viewport 390x844, /create tab): seeded a device via PATCH /api/auth/me + localStorage @groupup/device_id, filled title 'Vendo Drog3' + category 'basket' + location 'Parco' + tapped [data-testid=create-submit] — the inline [data-testid=create-error] appeared with the EXACT expected Italian message BEFORE any network call (client-side moderation via /app/frontend/src/lib/moderation.ts). Then re-tested with clean title 'Cena carbonara' — no moderation error, the group was actually created and the app navigated to /group/{id} (visual confirmation via screenshot). Both required user-facing behaviors verified. Backend full regression: 115/118 pass (9 TestExpiredGroupPurge pre-existing flaky tests deselected). The 3 failures are NOT introduced by this iteration and are documented in Issues: (a) English plural 'drugs galore' is not blocked because there is no 'drug' stem (only Italian 'drog'); the previous exact-word moderation covered it — this is a MODERATION GAP; (b, c) two TestPublicUserProfile tests expected 404 for non-existent target but now correctly get 403 (privacy nit from iteration_9 was applied to server.py) — the tests are stale, not the code.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py::_normalize_text is well-defined: leet map → collapse 3+ repeats → strip non-alpha → glue single-letter runs. Terminates because the string strictly shrinks (comment matches behavior).

server.py::_STEMS_RE uses \b at the START of each stem only — correct choice: it catches obfuscated tails (drog3, drog4, drogaaa) while avoiding mid-word false-positives (carmine ≠ armi, ceramica ≠ armi, sessione ≠ sesso, cocacola ≠ cocain, hashtag ≠ hashish).
moderation.ts::findForbiddenWord builds a fresh RegExp inside a for-loop per call. Minor perf nit: pre-compile once at module load. Non-blocking.
moderation.ts and server.py stem lists appear IDENTICAL — this is critical for UX (mirror the server rule client-side). Verified by inspection.
Backend applies _reject_if_forbidden to title/description/location/category_label in create_group and to text in post_message. Coverage matches the spec.

MODERATION GAP: English 'drug' is not a stem. Also 'meth' is not (only 'metanfet'/'methamph'). The clean-word test 'Metodo di studio' passes precisely because there is no 'meth' stem; if the user later adds 'meth' as a stem, 'Metodo' would be a NEW false positive.
server.py detail message correctly matches moderation.ts client message word-for-word — verified by explicit test_forbidden_detail_message_exact.
